text:
Toronto is 8-7-2 with a plus-7 goal differential, and the second number flatters the first. The Leafs have taken 47% of the expected goals (45% at five on five), but they have scored 62 times on 51.9 expected, more than 10 goals above what their chances suggest. The goaltending has helped too, 55 allowed against 59.2 expected. Our simulations still give them only a 16% playoff chance, because the process underneath the record is that of a team below .500.

The hot hand is Jack Roslovic, with 13 points in his last 10 games against 7.5 expected. Next to Auston Matthews and Easton Cowan, that line has outscored teams 7-2 in 59 minutes. Swap in Kirill Marchenko and the chance share jumps to 69%, so whoever plays the right wing, the Matthews line is driving.

The worry is the blue line and the box. Both regular pairs, Jake McCabe with Darren Raddysh and Morgan Rielly with Troy Stecher, sit at 45% of the chances. The Leafs take 4.47 penalties a game, and their penalty kill is allowing 0.83 expected goals a game.

Help arrives Saturday. Jim Hiller confirmed John Tavares returns against Montreal, and Daily Faceoff Toronto reported Matthews calling Tavares the best player on the ice at practice. Toronto needs another centre who tilts the ice. If Tavares is that, the luck has time to fade without the record following it.
headline: The Leafs are outscoring their chances
